correctness.rationale: The event AB nilpotent is equivalent to tr(AB)=0 and det A det B=0 in two dimensions. The traceless nilpotent cone has q² points, every nonzero nilpotent A is conjugate to E12, and intersection on that cone has q points. Inclusion-exclusion gives total 2q⁴+q³−3q²+q. The zero product stratum has 3q³−q²−q points by annihilator dimensions. Split/nonsplit odd characteristic and scalar/nonscalar even characteristic fibers follow by explicit matrix equations and elementary orbit sizes. The packaged independent brute-force checker exhausts q=2,3,4,5,7,9. Assumptions, finite-field constraints, nonzero/product distinctions and unproved limits were checked.

value.rationale: Nilpotent-product probability on a natural traceless three-dimensional matrix space tests the stability of ring-level probabilistic invariants under trace constraints. Exact arithmetic fiber trichotomies expose nontrivial finite-field splitting versus characteristic-two singularity, while the total universal polynomial and exact zero/nonzero decomposition have their own structural mathematical meaning. The invariant is naturally specified, is not a routine parameter renaming of the full-ring theorem, and supports subsequent questions for prescribed traces and higher matrix dimensions.
